title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: A Paired Study under Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CAND-2026-001) that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired contingency counts n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 (exact binomial-tail convention). Paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI for the absolute risk difference = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement arose from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a multi-step required-sequence ordering violation in an extreme-difficulty task (required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3). We report preregistration, full execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), paired analysis, a diagnostic of the repaired pair from archived validator traces, and evidence-grounded limitations and implications.

sections.introduction: Translating high-level operator intent into device configurations (intent→config) is a canonical NetOps use case proposed for large language models (LLMs). Operational correctness requires generated artifacts to satisfy deterministic invariants—ordering constraints, group-level safety, and syntactic/semantic per-device constraints—that can be checked by a verifier before deployment. Prior prototype work motivates verifier-aware pipelines and generate→validate→repair patterns but leaves open how much additional verifier-triggered bounded repair changes acceptance when the identical initial sample is reused across comparison conditions. To isolate the marginal effect of a single permitted automated repair, we conducted a preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each task the identical single sampled candidate was deterministically reused by both baseline (no repair) and guarded (verifier may trigger ≤1 repair) episodes, so any paired difference arises only from the permitted validator-triggered repair.
sections.related_work:
Recent work has prototyped intent→configuration systems and benchmark-style evaluations showing feasibility for LLM-driven NetOps workflows [1]. Deterministic configuration verification methods provide operational oracles appropriate for evaluating syntactic and semantic invariants in generated configurations [2]. In adjacent domains, generate→validate→repair and test-in-the-loop program-repair studies demonstrate that validating generated artifacts against executable checks and applying bounded repairs can remedy some classes of generator errors [4]. Tool-augmented agent designs and LLM+tool studies demonstrate engineering patterns for coupling generators to external solvers and verifiers; those works motivate verifier-integrated NetOps pipelines but do not quantify repair-only effects under paired shared-candidate semantics [6]. Reporting and preregistration guidelines informed the experimental design and archival choices for a reproducible confirmatory analysis [3],[5].

Synthesis and gap. The supplied literature collectively supports (i) active prototyping of intent→config pipelines [1], (ii) suitability of deterministic verifiers as operational oracles for syntactic and ordering invariants [2], and (iii) promise of generate→validate→repair patterns in adjacent domains albeit without NetOps-specific paired evidence measuring repair-only effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics [4],[6]. Our experiment addresses that narrow empirical gap by quantifying the marginal repair effect when both conditions begin from the identical generated candidate.
sections.methodology:
Design and preregistration. The design and analysis plan were preregistered (CAND-2026-001) and fixed prior to any model calls. Key preregistered elements: paired binary estimand (per-task deterministic-verifier acceptance, baseline vs guarded), deterministic task sampling (N=200), generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task reused by both episodes), ≤1 automated repair per task, primary failed-call treatment complete_pair_primary, confirmatory exact two-sided McNemar test (exact binomial-tail implementation), and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistration and all artifacts are archived in the execution bundle.

Task generator and verifier oracle. Tasks came from a deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) with fixed selection indices. Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence ordering, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow_policies. The deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses generated commands, enforces allowed_fields and required_sequence, evaluates group-level invariants (final_group_constraints, minimum_active_in_groups), and returns a Boolean full_intent_constraint_validation only when all encoded constraints are satisfied. The verifier emits structured tracer output archived and used as the authoritative scoring artifact.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and sampling. The adapter contract enforced that for each pair the exact same single sampled candidate was provided to both baseline and guarded episodes. Under those semantics any paired difference can only arise from the deterministic verifier and the single permitted repair; it cannot arise from independent guarded first-pass generations, prompt differences, or selection among multiple samples. The model-configuration record declares requested_model = gpt-5-mini and records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly state that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; nondeterministic hosted-model sampling therefore remains a background possibility even though the experiment used a single initial sample per pair by design.

Sanitizer, repair policy, and call accounting. Each initial generation passed a deterministic formatting sanitizer before verifier parsing. If the verifier found violations, the guarded logic could invoke at most one automated repair call constructed from the verifier trace. Repair calls were counted against the model-call budget; deterministic reconciliation records stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1} and hosted_model_call_event_count = 201. Primary analysis followed complete_pair_primary; sensitivity handling for persistent unparsables was preregistered but not invoked because no persistent unparsables occurred.

Statistical procedures. The primary test is the exact two-sided McNemar test computed from discordant pair counts n10 and n01 using the exact binomial-tail convention (p = 2 × min{BinomCDF(k; n, 0.5), 1 − BinomCDF(k − 1; n, 0.5)} with n = n10 + n01 and k = n10). With small discordant counts this exact-binomial convention is the preregistered confirmatory procedure. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute risk difference used 10,000 resamples and bootstrap_seed = 1729; bootstrap settings are archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The run completed in ≈29 minutes (start 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00, end 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00). planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0. Provider-call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}; cache_miss_count = 201 and cache_hit_count = 0.

Confirmatory outcomes. From archived analysis artifacts: baseline successes = 199, baseline failures = 1 (baseline success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200, guarded failures = 0 (guarded success_rate = 1.0). Contingency table: n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact two-sided McNemar p-value (n = 1, k = 1 under the preregistered convention) = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute risk difference (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) = [0.00, 0.015]. These numbers reproduce from the archived analysis executor.

Repaired pair diagnostic. The guarded pipeline invoked exactly one automated repair. Archived validator traces for the repaired pair show the shared initial candidate violated the task's required_sequence ordering constraint: the task manifest difficulty metadata for that pair recorded required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3, difficulty.level = "extreme". The verifier tracer documents validation_before.violation_codes indicating an ordering breach and validation_after.valid = true once the bounded repair was applied. The repair converted a sequenced-dependency failure into a configuration accepted by the deterministic verifier; scorer returned score = 1 with scorer_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION". These validator-trace fields are the archived evidence that the single observed paired improvement resulted from the verifier-triggered repair that enacted the required reordering.

Representative diagnostics. Representative task manifests in the archive show required_command_count values spanning 3–9 and changed_interface_count up to 3 across examples. The lone baseline failure is associated with an extreme composite difficulty profile (required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3), consistent with the preregistered exploratory hypothesis that multi-device sequencing and dependency complexity concentrate residual failures.
sections.discussion:
What the estimand measures. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics both baseline and guarded episodes begin from the identical sampled candidate; therefore the executed estimand isolates the marginal effect of permitting a single automated repair on that candidate. The comparison does not measure benefits that would arise from independent guarded first-pass generations, different prompt templates, or selection among multiple model samples; any paired difference arises solely from the verifier and the single permitted repair.

Statistical regime and interpretation. The realized baseline success rate (199/200 = 99.5%) yields a sparse-discordant regime (n = n10 + n01 = 1). With only one discordant pair the exact McNemar p-value (preregistered exact-binomial convention) equals p = 1.0, providing no strong directional confirmatory evidence under the small-discordant count. The paired-bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.015] quantifies uncertainty and bounds the plausible absolute improvement attributable to repair under the repair-only estimand: the data are compatible with at most a small absolute improvement (≤1.5 percentage points) in this experiment. Thus, despite a point estimate favoring the guarded pipeline by 0.005, the dataset's high baseline ceiling restricts sensitivity to detect small repair-only effects at N = 200.

Failure-mode interpretation. The single repaired case illustrates a class of errors that a verifier-triggered bounded repair can address: concrete required-sequence ordering violations where the verifier exposes an explicit, repairable sequence mismatch. The archived tracer shows the repair prompt derived from the verifier trace produced a corrected ordering that satisfied all manifest-encoded invariants. In contrast, the verifier cannot detect or repair errors outside its encoded oracle (dataplane-only behaviors, vendor runtime quirks not reflected in the manifest). Representative diagnostics suggest that residual failures concentrate in tasks with high required_command_count and multiple changed interfaces, supporting the preregistered exploratory expectation that multi-device sequencing complexity concentrates risk.

Threats to validity. Internal: shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolate repair effects but do not assess prompt sensitivity, sampling variability, or multi-sample selection trade-offs. The model-configuration record records temperature = null/unset; that is not evidence of deterministic sampling and therefore nondeterministic hosted-model sampling remains a background property. Construct: the deterministic verifier enforces manifest-encoded invariants but is not a substitute for dataplane emulation or vendor-specific runtime testing. External: a single-model run (gpt-5-mini) on a synthetic deterministic task bank limits generality to other models, real vendor templates, and production topologies. Statistical: with only one discordant pair, power to detect small absolute repair-only effects is limited; the paired-bootstrap CI reports that uncertainty.

Operationally bounded implications and future validation. Artifact-grounded evidence supports a narrow conclusion: in this synthetic deterministic task set, with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, a verifier-triggered bounded repair corrected a localized multi-step ordering fault in one extreme task. This is direct evidence that verifier-guided bounded repair can remedy certain ordering/dependency violations when those violations are expressible in the task manifest’s invariants. It is not evidence that bounded repair will correct dataplane-only defects, scale across heterogeneous vendor semantics, or generalize across models. Concrete next empirical steps (not executed here) include: multi-model paired studies, experiments that permit independent guarded first-pass generations to measure sample-selection benefits, adversarial/poisoning contamination experiments, and live-device or dataplane emulation to evaluate runtime semantics—each of which is outside the completed execution evidence and therefore remains future work.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment measuring the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered bounded repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In 200 synthetic deterministic tasks with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, baseline acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation (extreme difficulty task with required_command_count = 9 and changed_interface_count = 3). Paired absolute risk difference = 0.005, paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729), and exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics this evidence quantifies a repair-only effect: verifier-guided bounded repair can correct localized ordering faults in a synthetic verifier-backed setting, but broader operational claims require further empirical validation using the experiments described above.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Deterministic verifier (oracle): deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Archived provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are available in the execution bundle for audit.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
